title: R-Controlled Vowel Sounds
keyIdea: When r comes right after a vowel, the vowel and the r make one new sound together. ar says the sound in car and farm. or says the sound in fork and corn, and ore at the end of a word says the same sound, as in more. ir, ur and er all say the same sound, as in bird, burn and her, so you have to learn which spelling each word uses. Adding r changes the word: cat becomes cart, bun becomes burn. Two letters, one sound: bird has four letters but three sounds, b, ir, d.
familyTip: Go on an r hunt in a picture book. Your child finds words like car, star, corn, bird or her, and puts a finger under the vowel and the r together while saying the one sound. Then play 'add an r': say cat, and ask what you get with r after the a (cart). Try bun to burn and shot to short.

visual.caption: Which sound does each word have? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: slide an r in after the vowel to make new words, sort words by sound, tap the letters that make the sound, and pick the right spelling.

kid: Look at cat. Now put an r after the a. You get cart. The a and the r say a new sound together: ar.
ar says the sound in car and star. or says the sound in fork and corn. ore says it too, like in more.
ir, ur and er all say the same sound. Listen: bird, burn, her. They sound the same, but they look different. We learn which one each word has.
Two letters, one sound. In bird, i and r go together. So bird has four letters but three sounds: b, ir, d.
adult: Ages 5 to 6. The National Curriculum in England teaches these graphemes in Year 1 (English Appendix 1): ar (car, start, park, arm, garden), or (for, short, born, horse, morning), ore (more, score, before, wore, shore), er (her, term, verb, person), ir (girl, bird, shirt, first, third) and ur (turn, hurt, church, burst, Thursday). In US phonics these are r-controlled vowels (Common Core RF.1.3 and RF.2.3), and a syllable with one is an r-controlled syllable.

The r changes the vowel, so the vowel and r are read as one phoneme. In standard British English the r is not sounded separately at all; in American English it is blended into the vowel. Either way, cart has three phonemes, c, ar, t, not four. ir, ur and er spell the same sound, so the spelling of each word has to be learned and checked; in most words er comes at the end (her, letter) while ir and ur come in the middle.

Common mistakes: reading the short vowel and then a separate r (c-a-r-t as four sounds, or reading cart as cat), reversing the letters (crat, gril, hrut), choosing the wrong one of ir, ur and er (gurl, nirse, burd), writing or for ore at the end (mor), and counting letters instead of sounds when segmenting.

In the lab your child slides an r tile into four short words to make new ones (cat to cart, bun to burn, bid to bird, shot to short), sorts nine words into ar, or and er sound boxes, taps the letters that make the sound in six words, picks ir or ur, or or ar for four gaps, and decides in five sentences whether the word needs an r.

practice.prompt: Which word has the same sound as car?
practice.hint: Find the word with a and r together.
practice.explain: farm has ar, the sound in car. fork has or, and fan has no r.

practice.prompt: A word has {n} letters. Two of them are a and r together, and every other letter makes its own sound. How many sounds does the word have?
practice.hint: a and r make one sound, so two letters count as one.
practice.explain: {n} letters, but ar counts once, so {=n-1} sounds. car has 3 letters and 2 sounds: c, ar.

practice.prompt: bird, burn and her. What is the same?
practice.hint: Say them out loud. Then look at the letters.
practice.explain: ir, ur and er make the same sound, but they are spelt with different letters.

practice.prompt: A word has {n} letters, like bun. You put r right after the vowel, like burn. How many letters does the new word have?
practice.hint: You add one letter. Count it.
practice.explain: {n} letters plus the r gives {=n+1} letters. The number of sounds stays {n}, because u and r say one sound.

practice.hint: ir and ur sound the same. Which one does girl use? The r comes after the vowel.
practice.explain: girl is spelt g, ir, l. gurl has the wrong letters for the sound, and gril has the r before the i.

pool.prompt: Put r after the a in cat. What word do you get?
pool.hint: The r goes right after the vowel a.
pool.explain: c, a, r, t: cart. The a and the r make one sound, ar.

pool.prompt: Which word has the same sound as fork?
pool.hint: Look for o and r together.
pool.explain: corn has or, like fork. card has ar and curl has ur.

pool.prompt: Which letters make one sound in shirt?
pool.hint: Find the vowel with r right after it.
pool.explain: i and r go together: sh, ir, t. sh is a different sound.

pool.prompt: A word has {n} letters and ends in ore, like more. Every other letter makes its own sound. How many sounds does it have?
pool.hint: o, r and e make one sound together, so three letters count as one.
pool.explain: {n} letters, but ore counts once, so {=n-2} sounds. more has 4 letters and 2 sounds: m, ore.

pool.prompt: Mia has {a} cards with ir words, {b} with ur words and {c} with er words. How many cards say the same sound as her?
pool.hint: ir, ur and er all say the same sound.
pool.explain: All three spellings say the sound in her, so {a} + {b} + {c} = {=a+b+c} cards.

pool.hint: Which word means it gives you pain?
pool.explain: hurt has ur. hut is a little house, and hurd is not a word.

pool.prompt: She looks after sick people. Which spelling is right?
pool.hint: ir and ur sound the same. nurse uses one of them, after the vowel.
pool.explain: nurse is spelt n, ur, se. nirse has the wrong letters, and nruse has the r too soon.

pool.prompt: How many sounds are in star?
pool.hint: s, t, then a and r together.
pool.explain: star has 4 letters but 3 sounds: s, t, ar.

pool.prompt: The pet that says meow is a ...
pool.hint: Does this word need an r?
pool.explain: A cat says meow. cart has an r and means something with wheels.

pool.prompt: Which word ends with the same sound as more?
pool.hint: Look for o, r, e at the end.
pool.explain: shore ends in ore, like more. share ends in are, and sure sounds different.
